summary: The candidate captures the principal definitions, main theorems, auxiliary lemmas, and most cited external results, with generally accurate mathematical statements and page numbers. However, several entries are materially incomplete or misclassified: the Bauer–Furuta invariant definition is only a fragment, the Bauer connected-sum nonvanishing result is reduced to an unspecified condition, the symplectic-structure definition from the gold artifact is missing, and the embedded-sphere lemma uses a different homology-class expression than the gold reference. Corollaries are repeatedly typed as theorems, and Lemmas 2.6 and 3.1 are duplicated under separate IDs, reducing precision and redundancy control.
strengths: All core gold results, including Theorems 1.4, 1.9, 2.3, 2.4 and the homology-class lemma, have recognizable candidate counterparts.
The 2-handle-neighborhood definition, positivity condition, Frøyshov vanishing result, Taubes nonvanishing result, and Betti-parity fact are substantially accurate.
Most entries retain useful theorem numbers and page locators, and external attribution is explicitly marked for several background results.
issues: The stable cohomotopy/Bauer–Furuta invariant definition is drastically under-specified compared with the gold statement.
The Bauer connected-sum theorem is not extracted as its own gold-matching entry and its second hypothesis is summarized vaguely as '文中列出的连通和条件,' omitting substantive conditions.
The gold symplectic-structure definition is absent.

The embedded-sphere lemma is represented using alpha-minus-bar-alpha in duplicate entries, whereas the gold entry specifies the class alpha times bar-alpha; this is a substantive statement mismatch relative to the reference.
Corollaries 1.5, 1.6, 1.7 and 2.5 are typed as theorem entries rather than being distinguished as corollaries/claims.
Lemmas 2.6 and 3.1 are duplicated under multiple IDs, creating avoidable redundancy and weakening locator/identity precision.
Some congruence formulas scope the mod-4 qualifier ambiguously, even though the intended conditions are inferable.
